title: Cryptography
body:
The [[THE NEW TURING OMNIBUS|Omnibus]] chapter on cryptography. It is one chapter, and MATH 4111
is a whole term on the same subject, so **this note is a pointer and [[CRYPTOGRAPHY]] holds the
material.**

> [!note] Not a duplicate
> `Books/Cryptography.md` (this note) and `MATH 4TH YEAR/MATH 4111/CRYPTOGRAPHY.md` differ only in
> case. Obsidian resolves each to itself, so both links work, but they are not two treatments of
> one topic: this is the book chapter, that is the course.

What the chapter covers, and where it went:

| Chapter topic | Note |
|---|---|
| Substitution and the Caesar cipher | [[Classical Ciphers]] |
| Breaking them by letter counts | [[Cryptanalysis]] |
| One-way functions and trapdoors | [[Public Key Cryptography]] |
| RSA and the difficulty of factoring | [[RSA]] |

Two of the book's neighbouring chapters are the same mathematics doing different jobs, which is the
reason the Omnibus puts them near each other:

- [[Random Numbers]] is the generator problem. A [[Stream Cipher]] is a pseudo-random generator
  strong enough that predicting the next bit is infeasible, and every practical difference between
  the two is that one word.
- [[Error Correcting Code]] is [[Finite Field]] algebra pointed at **noise** rather than at an
  adversary. Same polynomials over $GF(2^8)$ that [[AES]] uses, run to repair a corrupted byte
  instead of to hide one. Code-based [[Post-Quantum Cryptography]] closes the loop by turning
  decoding back into a hardness assumption.
